name: African Daisy
grown_as: A tender perennial from South Africa, in the UK grown as a summer annual or kept under glass in winter. William's library lists Osteospermum ecklonis 'Pink Sun'. Drawn with pink rays and a dark blue-purple centre. ⚠️ CHECK the colour: the wild species is white with a blue centre, and no description of 'Pink Sun' could be found.
habit: A low, mounded to spreading plant 30 to 60 cm high, woody at the base, the stems and leaves slightly sticky.

leaf.outline: Oblong to spoon-shaped (widest beyond the middle), 4 to 10 cm
leaf.base: Narrowing to the stem without a proper stalk
leaf.margin: A few widely spaced, coarse teeth, or smooth
leaf.veins: A clear midrib; side veins faint
leaf.surface: Slightly fleshy, finely hairy and a little sticky

flower.petals: About 12 to 20 broad, oblong ray florets with rounded tips, slightly glossy, spreading flat; the backs often darker
flower.centre: A dark blue-purple to navy disc dotted with yellow pollen
flower.behind: One or two rows of narrow, pointed green bracts
flower.carried: Alone on long stalks above the leaves, facing up; closes at night and in dull weather

fruit: Only the outer (ray) florets make seed, so a ring of hard seeds forms at the edge of the closed, withered head. Seeds bony, ridged and warty, grey-brown, 5 to 7 mm.
seedling: Two oblong seed leaves. The first true leaves are oblong with a few teeth.
winter: Usually lost to frost outdoors in the UK; may survive a mild winter in a sheltered spot.

leaf: a few widely spaced coarse teeth
bloom: one ring of broad rays with rounded tips
dark blue-purple centre with yellow pollen dots
flower: many daisies on long stalks above, facing up
seedhead: a ring of hard seeds at the edge

look_alikes: Cape marigold (Dimorphotheca sinuata) is a smaller annual, usually orange. Gazania has rays with dark rings near the base and leaves white beneath. Ox-eye daisy has a yellow centre.
